Method: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/repro_idea_search.py extracts lines 258-298 (the per-arm loop) and 301-339 (the heads/efficiency block) VERBATIM from /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py, dedents the 4 spaces of `with slot():`, and execs them against stubs that copy the real behaviour (n_gen = max(1, ceil(budget/population)) from gp.py:735; checkpoints named archive_gen{generation:03d}.csv written after every generation with checkpoint_every=1 from gp.py:874; ParturaScorer appending itself to SCORERS only at the END of __init__, after the raise, idea_search.py:132-136). So the code that ran is the code under review.

(a) CONFIRMED, and stronger than reported. A run that OOMs in generation 3 and a run that completes all 4 generations produce evidence["arms"]["steer"] dicts that are identical apart from wall-clock `seconds`/`scoring_seconds` (harness prints `evidence identical apart from wall-clock timings: True`). No field name in the arm dict contains err/gen/complete/status — the harness prints NONE. The archive being unchanged across the last generations is not contrived: the script's own docstring (lines 219-223) says e1's steer arm spent most of its budget on re-wrappings of one seed, all with the same score.

My best refutation attempt was that `scored` could be compared against the top-level `budget` to spot a short run. It fails on two counts: (i) gp.py mine() scores one population BEFORE the loop plus n_gen more, so a complete 192/48 run touches 5*48=240 trees, yet (ii) GPMiner._score caches by structural key (gp.py:424-435), so the real completed run at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/episodes/e1_I2_dispersion_fold/evidence.json recorded scored=123 against budget=192 (control 170). `scored` is therefore uninformative about completion — 123 of 192 is what a healthy run looks like there.

(a2) CONFIRMED. make_scorer is called at gp.py:320, which is inside GPMiner.__init__ (lines 159-357, verified by AST), i.e. inside run_mining, i.e. inside the try. The patch reaches it: gp.py binds make_scorer as a module global at line 47 and calls it as a bare global, and idea_search.py:173 rebinds agp.make_scorer. With the grid RuntimeError raised in __init__ the scorer never reaches SCORERS.append, so the harness records both arms as scored 0 / gate_fail 0 / archive 0 / live 0 / passers 0 / candidates [], evidence.json is written, and the process exits 0.

(b) CONFIRMED. Nothing ever cleans the directory: pipeline.py:351 only computes ckpt_dir and gp.py:239-240/873 only mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); study.sh's `idea` target (lines 173-174) launches with no cleanup and TAG defaults to "e1", so a re-run of the same idea lands in the same episodes/<tag>_<idea>/<arm>/checkpoints. Harness: run 1 at --budget 384 leaves archive_gen001..008 with three passers; run 2 at --budget 192 writes gen001..004 with none; `files[-1]` picks archive_gen008.csv, and the arm is recorded as archive 3 / live 3 / passers 3 with candidates ['day_fold_disp(Ret, 20)', 'day_std_ratio(Ret, 5, 60)', 'day_qrange(Ret, 20)'] — expressions this run never produced — while scored=123 comes from the new run's in-process counter. Running the real tail block then yields independent_distinct=3 and efficiency_per_100=2.4, literally 100 * (3 heads from the 384 run) / (123 evaluations of the 192 run).

(b2) An extra trigger the report did not list, same root cause: the budget need not drop. A re-run at the SAME budget that dies in generation 3 overwrites gen001-002 and leaves the previous run's gen003-004 in place, so files[-1]=archive_gen004.csv and the arm is recorded with 3 passers although it passed nothing. `--population` going up with the budget fixed does it too (n_gen=ceil(budget/pop) shrinks).

Why this changes conclusions rather than being cosmetic: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/guidance_report.py:146-158 renders A['scored'], A['live'], A['passers'], A.get('independent_distinct'), A.get('efficiency_per_100') and the per-arm `heads` expression list straight into the report table, with no validation — so a crashed arm appears as a clean negative on steering, and a stale arm appears as discoveries credited to the wrong budget. Also note evidence.json is written at the end of each arm iteration (line 298), so the misleading file is on disk even if the process later dies in the tail block; study.sh idea-pull will fetch it.

result.corrected_fix:
The finding stands, but suggestion (1) as written is dead code and (2) is not implementable as stated.

(1) `except Exception as exc: evidence["arms"][arm] = {..., "error": ...}` would be overwritten: line 293 unconditionally reassigns evidence["arms"][arm] a few lines later. Stash the error instead and merge it at line 293:

    err = None
    try:
        run_mining(...)
    except Exception as exc:                     # noqa: BLE001
        err = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc)[:300]}"
        print(f"[idea] {arm}: run_mining ended with {err}", flush=True)

and in the arm dict add: "error": err, "generations": len(files), "generations_expected": max(1, math.ceil(BUDGET / POP)), "scorers": len(SCORERS) - n0. With checkpoint_every=1 and rolling_block=0 a complete run writes exactly ceil(BUDGET/POP) files, so generations != generations_expected is the completion test. Record it; do NOT `assert len(files) == n_gen` as suggested — an assert throws away the salvageable archive the except clause exists to keep, and is a no-op under python -O.

(2) Do not move the grid assertion before run_mining — the GP's label grid is built inside run_mining (pipeline.py builds the view and target before constructing GPMiner), so there is nothing to compare ctx.tgt against until then without duplicating the whole view build. Make the failure fatal instead, right after the except, since in that case there is nothing to salvage:

    if err and not files:
        sys.exit(f"[idea] {arm}: nothing was scored and no checkpoint was written -- {err}")

(The scorer-construction failure is exactly this case: no scorer registered, no checkpoint. Optionally also `if err and len(SCORERS) == n0: sys.exit(...)`.)

(3) Clearing the arm directory is right, but it must happen before run_mining writes anything, and `shutil` is not currently imported (lines 24-32). Put it immediately before `install(arm)` in the arm loop:

    shutil.rmtree(ep_dir / arm, ignore_errors=True)

Prefer this over timestamping run_id: the arm name is what the log lines and the evidence keys refer to, and a timestamped dir would grow without bound on the server.

(4) Also pick the checkpoint numerically rather than lexicographically, so the choice survives a generation count that overflows 3 digits: `files = sorted((ep_dir / arm / "checkpoints").glob("archive_gen*.csv"), key=lambda p: int(p.stem[len("archive_gen"):]))`.

(5) Downstream, /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/guidance_report.py:153-156 should mark or skip an arm whose "error" is set or whose generations < generations_expected; otherwise the report still presents a crash as a negative result on steering.
